Decision: Existing-family control; do not count as new alpha
Authors: Lasse de la Porte-Simonsen; Ralph Sueppel
Economic_intuition: Repeated unexpected releases may diffuse into economic views and policy expectations.
Required_inputs: First-release actual, pre-release consensus, release timestamp, indicator direction and prior surprise history.
Construction: Proposed monthly adaptation: s_j=(actual_j-consensus_j)/SD(prior surprises_j); x_m=mean of sign-aligned s_j released in month m. Compare with existing aggregation before adding. Source uses model-implied surprises and a 5-trading-day half-life, not this monthly consensus formula.
Definition_status: Proposed adaptation; source method is different and precisely described
Horizon: Source: next-day; proposed: next month
Reported_evidence: Provider reports daily predictive relationships across markets, 2000–June 2026; not evidence for monthly predictability.
Independent_verification: Source reviewed; no independent replication or BNY backtest performed
Historical_data_access: Official actuals via BLS/BEA/Census and ALFRED vintages. Long consensus archive requires existing export/licensed source; free official actuals do not supply consensus.
Point_in_time_requirements: Keep first print and forecast timestamp; never compute surprise SD on the full sample. Revision events are distinct observations.
Monthly_MVP_fit: Easy if existing event table is available; no code/data inspected.
Incremental_information: Very high overlap with stated macro-surprise/growth/inflation baseline.
Main_limitations: Announcement effects can be exhausted before month-end; duplicate information; forecast survey bias; smoothing/window search.
Causal_RAG_role: Explain which surprise-to-policy links have contemporaneous documentary support; do not manufacture a replacement numerical surprise.

Decision: Reserve; inspect existing interaction terms
Authors: Antonio Gil de Rubio Cruz; Emilio Osambela; Dino Palazzo; Francisco Palomino; Gustavo Suarez
Economic_intuition: Inflation news can have a different discount-rate impact when inflation expectations and demand are elevated.
Required_inputs: Existing CPI/PCE surprise; latest available inflation expectation or core inflation state; optional real-time growth state.
Construction: Proposed one-term feature x_m = inflation_surprise_m * z_train(latest_available_core_PCE_YoY_m). Select this state in advance; do not also search many thresholds. This is not a replication of the paper.
Definition_status: Proposed adaptation; exact paper specification not reproduced
Horizon: Source: announcement response; proposed: next month
Reported_evidence: Authors report negative, state-dependent stock responses to inflation surprises. Does not establish delayed monthly alpha.
Independent_verification: Source reviewed; no independent replication or BNY backtest performed
Historical_data_access: Reuse surprise table; core PCE from BEA/FRED PCEPILFE with ALFRED vintages. Survey expectations may need licensed history.
Point_in_time_requirements: State must be released before decision; output gap estimates are especially revision-prone.
Monthly_MVP_fit: Easy once timestamps exist; add only if absent from factor interactions.
Incremental_information: Adds conditional mapping, not a new underlying information source.
Main_limitations: Small regime subsamples; state selection; multiple testing; event-day versus forward-return mismatch.
Causal_RAG_role: Useful for distinguishing growth-led from adverse inflation narratives using dated evidence, then testing a single predeclared interaction.

Decision: Reserve; high growth-factor overlap
Authors: Jordan Brooks
Economic_intuition: Gradual economic trends can persist and affect cash flows and policy before being fully priced.
Required_inputs: Real industrial production, real retail sales, and inflation histories with historical releases; asset-specific economic mapping.
Construction: Illustrative BNY proxy: 0.5*z_train(latest_released INDPRO YoY)+0.5*z_train(latest_released real retail sales YoY). The exact AQR multi-asset signal specification is not established by the landing page and requires the paper.
Definition_status: Requires source-level specification for replication; proxy explicitly proposed
Horizon: Monthly decisions; medium term
Reported_evidence: AQR describes a long multi-asset historical simulation with diversification benefits; no independent reproduction here.
Independent_verification: Source reviewed; no independent replication or BNY backtest performed
Historical_data_access: FRED INDPRO and RRSFS / Census sales deflated with available CPI; ALFRED vintages where available. Proprietary international implementations differ.
Point_in_time_requirements: Join on release dates, not observation month; rebuild historical transformations from the vintage available then.
Monthly_MVP_fit: Moderate; likely reuses growth inputs but historical vintages must be checked.
Incremental_information: Different from actual-minus-consensus surprises but likely overlaps growth-factor levels.
Main_limitations: Revisions, global-to-US transfer, release lag errors, mapping/weight selection and trend reversals.
Causal_RAG_role: Contextualize whether a trend reflects durable demand or a temporary disturbance; no need for an LLM to calculate growth rates.

Decision: Top five #2; first curve feature
Authors: mm123; PortfolioPerfection (community); compare Eric Engstrom and Steven Sharpe research
Economic_intuition: The curve contains expected policy-path and risk-premium information associated with the business cycle.
Required_inputs: Daily DGS10 and DGS3MO, or FRED T10Y3M; publication/availability timestamp.
Construction: x_m = last_available(T10Y3M, decision_time_m), in percentage points; standardize on each training window. Preserve continuous slope rather than optimize an inversion cutoff.
Definition_status: Slope is source-defined; continuous Ridge use is our proposed experiment
Horizon: Research: often 6–12 months; test next month first
Reported_evidence: Community explicitly admits fitting a lag to the last recession. Engstrom–Sharpe find near-term forward spread superior to longer spreads for macro/annual stock forecasts; simple slope remains a cheap challenger.
Independent_verification: Source reviewed; no independent replication or BNY backtest performed
Historical_data_access: https://fred.stlouisfed.org/series/T10Y3M ; long daily history since 1982; component yield histories via Treasury/FRED.
Point_in_time_requirements: Use values actually published before trading; a same-day observation is not automatically available at the close. Prefer next-session execution.
Monthly_MVP_fit: Low difficulty; one new monthly column if slope is absent.
Incremental_information: Expected policy path differs from release surprise; may already be captured by policy/curve features or ANFCI.
Main_limitations: Recession forecast is not stock-timing success; risk premia and QE distort slope; long variable leads; endogenous prices; crisis concentration.
Causal_RAG_role: Retrieve evidence for policy-easing expectations and growth concerns; curve inversion does not prove it causes recession.

Decision: Priority curve challenger after S04; data-vintage gate
Authors: Eric C. Engstrom; Steven A. Sharpe
Economic_intuition: Expected near-term rate easing can reveal deteriorating growth expectations with less long-duration term-premium contamination.
Required_inputs: Quarterly-maturity zero-coupon curve or six-quarter-ahead one-quarter forward Treasury rate and current one-quarter yield.
Construction: Original ntfs_t=fwd_t^6-y_t^1. For continuous annual zero yields z(T), a 1-quarter forward starting at 1.5 years is [1.75*z(1.75)-1.5*z(1.5)]/0.25; subtract z(0.25), with consistent units/conventions.
Definition_status: Source-defined; discount-curve expression is algebra, not a performance claim
Horizon: Original stock-return evidence: subsequent four quarters; monthly transfer unproven
Reported_evidence: Authors report incremental recession/GDP/stock-return information relative to long spreads; neither an independent replication nor proof for monthly ETF returns.
Independent_verification: Source reviewed; no independent replication or BNY backtest performed
Historical_data_access: Fed paper has accessible materials; https://www.federalreserve.gov/data/nominal-yield-curve.htm provides curve parameters since 1961. Current GSW curves are a possible reconstruction, not guaranteed exact original data.
Point_in_time_requirements: Fed curve estimates generally posted weekly after the observation dates; histories can change. Require archived vintages/posting dates or label reconstructed series pseudo-real-time.
Monthly_MVP_fit: Moderate; do not interpolate par yields as if they were zero-coupon rates. S04 is the separate low-cost first experiment.
Incremental_information: Policy expectations can be new; compare directly against S04 and existing policy variables without pooling both by default.
Main_limitations: Short-end curve fit excludes bills in GSW; curve-model revisions; horizon mismatch; lower bound; reverse causality; extra specification search.
Causal_RAG_role: High relevance to the spending→inflation→expected-rate-path chain. Documentary support does not identify an exogenous shock.

Decision: Top five #1; first credit feature
Authors: Victor1991; AlgoMan (community). Mechanism: Simon Gilchrist and Egon Zakrajsek (2012)
Economic_intuition: Widening credit spreads may reveal financing stress and weakening risk-bearing capacity before they appear in releases.
Required_inputs: BAA10Y daily spread; optional archived ICE HY OAS BAMLH0A0HYM2 as a separate robustness series.
Construction: Proposed x_m=c_m-c_(m-3), where c_m is last published BAA10Y before decision. Positive means widening. Let Ridge estimate return sign. Do not import community stock-beta allocation rule.
Definition_status: Our simple feature; community and credit literature motivate it, not validate this exact specification
Assets: Equity; duration; credit if already in universe
Horizon: Proposed next month; economic mechanism over 1–12 months
Reported_evidence: Community reports US/Europe differences and higher turnover. Gilchrist–Zakrajsek evidence chiefly concerns decomposed credit and macro activity; it does not validate this Baa proxy.
Independent_verification: Source reviewed; no independent replication or BNY backtest performed
Historical_data_access: https://fred.stlouisfed.org/series/BAA10Y is publicly viewable long history since 1986. HY OAS at https://fred.stlouisfed.org/series/BAMLH0A0HYM2 is restricted to 3 years from April 2026. Longer OAS needs authorized archive/provider.
Point_in_time_requirements: Retain availability lag; public access is not unrestricted redistribution. Baa-minus-Treasury has maturity, duration and composition mismatch; it is neither OAS nor EBP.
Monthly_MVP_fit: Low difficulty if curve/spread daily exports exist; one monthly column. Check exact existing features first.
Incremental_information: Credit-risk state versus macro-release news; likely partial ANFCI overlap.
Main_limitations: Stress momentum and high starting expected returns can imply different signs; not pure credit; crisis dominance; stale quotes; source changes; costs.
Causal_RAG_role: Validate whether widening coincides with funding stress, defaults, sector events or broad risk aversion using contemporaneous documents; never hard-code all widening as bearish.

Decision: Defer until historical vintages are defensible
Authors: Giovanni Favara; Simon Gilchrist; Kurt F. Lewis; Egon Zakrajsek
Economic_intuition: Non-default spread compensation may reflect intermediary risk appetite and financing conditions.
Required_inputs: Fed EBP monthly series and release archive; optionally original bond and firm data for recursive estimation.
Construction: Source EBP=GZ corporate spread minus fitted default-risk component. Proposed feature: last released EBP level; do not estimate it by BAA10Y minus another aggregate yield.
Definition_status: Original measure; monthly forecasting feature proposed
Horizon: Source: next-12-month recession risk; monthly returns unproven
Reported_evidence: Published research supports business-cycle forecasting. Fed warns entire EBP history may revise monthly; a free current CSV is not point-in-time data.
Independent_verification: Source reviewed; no independent replication or BNY backtest performed
Historical_data_access: https://www.federalreserve.gov/econres/notes/feds-notes/ebp_csv.csv ; published history begins January 1973; vintage archive availability not established.
Point_in_time_requirements: Usually after 10am on fourth business day, with blackout/source delays possible. September 2026 provider change documented. Require dated snapshots; a one-month lag does not remove revisions.
Monthly_MVP_fit: Easy numerically; hard to make historical test valid.
Incremental_information: Potentially cleaner credit component than S06 but correlated; do not add both initially.
Main_limitations: Re-estimation and balance-sheet revisions; model dependence; imperfect default-risk separation; revised-history leakage.
Causal_RAG_role: News evidence can explain credit stress; 2024 Understanding the Excess Bond Premium paper supports studying news topics, not trusting an LLM probability.

Decision: Top five #3; explicit proxy, not exact VRP replication
Authors: Tim Bollerslev; George Tauchen; Hao Zhou
Economic_intuition: Option-implied variance relative to recent realized variance may contain priced aggregate uncertainty and risk compensation.
Required_inputs: Cboe VIX close and daily S&P 500 price returns, preferably same underlying; daily dates and publication cutoffs.
Construction: Our proxy x_m=(VIX_m/100)^2-(252/22)*sum_{k=0..21} r_(d_m-k)^2. Use log daily price returns, decimal units and last available close. True ex-ante VRP is risk-neutral expected future variance minus physical expected future variance; trailing variance is only a proxy.
Definition_status: Proposed implementable proxy; paper uses richer variance measurement
Assets: US equity; other asset forecasts exploratory
Horizon: Published evidence strongest around quarterly equity excess returns; test next month primary
Reported_evidence: Peer-reviewed evidence of equity-return predictability; no published result is asserted for this exact daily-close proxy or BNY universe.
Independent_verification: Source reviewed; no independent replication or BNY backtest performed
Historical_data_access: https://www.cboe.com/tradable-products/vix/vix-historical-data has 1990–present VIX history. Reuse team daily equity prices if available; long index data may require Bloomberg. Monthly prices cannot supply daily realized variance.
Point_in_time_requirements: VIX and underlying must both be observed before execution. Keep backfilled pre-2003 VIX methodology distinction; use daily calendar alignment and >22 past observations.
Monthly_MVP_fit: Moderate; daily prices are an additional requirement if MVP stores monthly returns only.
Incremental_information: Adds option-market pricing versus realized risk; likely distinct from macro surprises. Check incremental value beyond VIX level and realized variance separately.
Main_limitations: Proxy measurement error; variance-unit mismatch; volatility regimes; same-day trade leakage; crisis concentration; data cost/licensing.
Causal_RAG_role: Separate uncertainty narratives from economic surprise direction; evidence may contextualize risk compensation but cannot recover unobserved physical expectations.

Decision: Top five #4; second wave
Authors: Miguel Acosta; Andrea Ajello; Michael Bauer; Francesca Loria; Silvia Miranda-Agrippino
Economic_intuition: Unexpected policy communication changes the expected short-rate path and discount rates; information effects can change interpretation.
Required_inputs: USMPD event timestamps and supplied surprise outputs/code; FOMC event-type labels.
Construction: Source surprise: first PC of money-market futures rate changes over roughly one-year horizon. Proposed monthly feature: sum of non-overlapping monetary-event surprises in month; no-event month=0 only after coverage verified. Freeze PCA/loadings with training-only estimation for strict historical replication.
Definition_status: Source shock measure; monthly aggregation proposed
Horizon: Source: intraday event effects; monthly persistence is a hypothesis
Reported_evidence: New public database/research document event effects. It does not demonstrate a profitable monthly policy-shock strategy.
Independent_verification: Source reviewed; no independent replication or BNY backtest performed
Historical_data_access: https://www.frbsf.org/research-and-insights/data-and-indicators/us-monetary-policy-event-study-database/ ; Excel plus R code/output ZIP, page updated 2026-09-17. Check per-instrument start dates and original vintages.
Point_in_time_requirements: New public data publication in late 2025 differs from underlying historical market observability. Treat retrospective reconstruction separately from implementable data access. Do not double-count statement+press conference and combined monetary event.
Monthly_MVP_fit: Moderate; event-to-month adapter; source-estimated PC may embed full-sample information.
Incremental_information: Adds market-implied unexpected policy rather than surprise in CPI/jobs. May overlap existing policy factor.
Main_limitations: Fed information effect; PCA fit leakage; sparse meetings; event-window methodology; no automatic delayed alpha.
Causal_RAG_role: Excellent testing-agent target: distinguish tightening from information news with dated statements. Text alone cannot prove shock exogeneity.

Decision: Top five #5; second wave with vintage gate
Authors: Adam Shapiro
Economic_intuition: The same inflation reading can imply different growth/policy/credit outcomes depending on its source.
Required_inputs: Supply-driven, demand-driven and ambiguous monthly PCE inflation contributions; release/vintage history; existing inflation surprise.
Construction: Source classification uses signs of unexpected category price and quantity changes from rolling regressions. Proposed one-column composition feature x_m=D_m-S_m in published contribution units; later test inflation_surprise*(D-S) as a separately registered interaction.
Definition_status: Original decomposition; forecasting transformation proposed
Horizon: Monthly available; proposed next month; source is decomposition not alpha study
Reported_evidence: Official research provides measurable economic decomposition, not an established monthly trading signal. Bonelli–Palazzo–Yamarthy 2025 independently motivates time-varying inflation sensitivity using different measures.
Independent_verification: Source reviewed; no independent replication or BNY backtest performed
Historical_data_access: FRBSF chart CSV links are public; inspect full downloadable history and vintages before claiming usable span. BEA detailed PCE histories needed for reconstruction.
Point_in_time_requirements: Latest-vintage PCE input revisions can affect labels. Use published release snapshots; alternatively reconstruct recursively with historical BEA vintages. Historical retro-labels are not automatically available then.
Monthly_MVP_fit: Moderate to high historical preparation; retain ambiguous category rather than force binary labels.
Incremental_information: Adds inflation composition beyond headline magnitude; more promising incremental channel than another CPI transform.
Main_limitations: Classification/model error; revisions; sparse regimes; no demonstrated delayed returns; decomposition is not identified structural causality.
Causal_RAG_role: Strongest explanatory RAG use: test whether dated evidence agrees with measured supply/demand classification and whether it improves forecast interactions.

Decision: Reserve; mechanism stronger than demonstrated alpha
Authors: Board of Governors / US Treasury; conceptual mechanism only
Publication_date: Continuously updated series; no original alpha paper established
Economic_intuition: Real discount rates can affect duration-sensitive assets, but contemporaneous repricing need not continue next month.
Required_inputs: 10-year TIPS real yield DFII10; optional nominal DGS10 for breakeven attribution.
Construction: Our hypothesis x_m=DFII10_m-DFII10_(m-3), standardized in training. No source performance is claimed for this transformation.
Definition_status: Proposed hypothesis, not source-validated signal
Assets: Equity; nominal/TIPS duration; gold only if universe permits
Horizon: Next-month hypothesis; valuation effects can be contemporaneous
Reported_evidence: Verified input definition, not an independently supported return-forecasting rule.
Independent_verification: Source reviewed; no independent replication or BNY backtest performed
Historical_data_access: https://fred.stlouisfed.org/series/DFII10 ; daily public history since 2003. Nominal curve source provides companion yields.
Point_in_time_requirements: Observe publication lag; TIPS liquidity and index composition matter; no future averages.
Monthly_MVP_fit: Low difficulty; one additional market series.
Incremental_information: Discount-rate decomposition may supplement inflation surprise, but likely overlaps nominal policy/curve information.
Main_limitations: Growth news can raise real yields and equity prices together; 2008 liquidity; shorter history; sign instability.
Causal_RAG_role: Retrieve evidence about growth, policy and liquidity contributions; avoid mechanically treating rising real yields as a bearish forecast.

Decision: Defer; estimated-history audit first
Authors: Tobias Adrian; Richard K. Crump; Emanuel Moench
Publication_date: 2013 model; continuously updated NY Fed estimates
Economic_intuition: Compensation for duration risk is distinct from expected future short rates.
Required_inputs: NY Fed ACM 10-year term premium and historical vintages, or recursively estimated yield factors.
Construction: Proposed x_m=last released ACM 10-year term premium. This is model-implied compensation, not an observable realized return or a guaranteed predictor.
Definition_status: Published model estimate; forecast use proposed
Horizon: Medium term; one-month use exploratory
Reported_evidence: Widely used term-structure decomposition; no monthly BNY performance claim. Current landing page did not expose complete data metadata in retrieval.
Independent_verification: Source reviewed; no independent replication or BNY backtest performed
Historical_data_access: NY Fed page public; confirm download, history span, estimation window and archived versions before use.
Point_in_time_requirements: Audit whether parameter estimation uses future samples. Do not assume a current historical estimate was available on its observation date.
Monthly_MVP_fit: Easy feature if vintages exist; otherwise expensive recursive reconstruction.
Incremental_information: Potential separation of expected policy and risk premia, but overlaps curve/yield features.
Main_limitations: Model uncertainty; revisions/full-sample estimation; market regime changes; horizon mismatch.
Causal_RAG_role: Explain supply/uncertainty hypotheses for term premium; RAG cannot observe an unidentifiable premium directly.

Decision: Defer; wrong initial horizon and extra estimation
Authors: John H. Cochrane; Monika Piazzesi
Economic_intuition: A tent-shaped forward-rate combination may reveal cyclical bond risk premia missed by slope alone.
Required_inputs: Consistent zero-coupon yields/forwards and one-year excess holding returns for 2–5 year bonds.
Construction: Original CP_t=gamma0+gamma1*y1_t+sum_{n=2..5} gamma_n*f_n_t, gamma fitted to average one-year excess returns. Estimate coefficients only on completed training targets; do not take full-sample fitted factor as historical input.
Definition_status: Original factor structure; coefficients require estimation
Horizon: Original 12-month holding returns; monthly adaptation requires new specification
Reported_evidence: Original paper reports in-sample R-squared up to 0.44; not a monthly OOS statistic, independently reproduced result, or a Sharpe ratio.
Independent_verification: Source reviewed; no independent replication or BNY backtest performed
Historical_data_access: Author paper https://web.stanford.edu/~piazzesi/cp.pdf ; Fed zero curve can support approximate reconstruction. Exact original bond data and vintages not obtained.
Point_in_time_requirements: Annual training labels must mature before refitting; overlapping targets require purge/robust inference; curve posting/revision audit.
Monthly_MVP_fit: High relative to S04; defer until simple curve test complete.
Incremental_information: Potential nonlinear curve-shape information, but may duplicate Ridge yield factors.
Main_limitations: Generated-regressor and full-sample leakage; annual-to-monthly transfer; overlapping returns; model instability.
Causal_RAG_role: Limited extra value for RAG beyond interpreting term-premium mechanisms; numeric estimation should remain conventional.

Decision: Audit existing baseline; no new feature by default
Authors: Federal Reserve Bank of Chicago
Economic_intuition: Broad financing conditions summarize stress not captured by a single macro release.
Required_inputs: Weekly published NFCI/ANFCI values and vintage/release dates.
Construction: Source index is a mixed-frequency factor of financial indicators; proposed x_m=latest released index (not an additional homemade composite). Consider change only if separately registered.
Definition_status: Official source index; forecast use proposed
Horizon: Monthly decision using weekly input
Reported_evidence: Chicago Fed documents historical changes from new inputs, revisions and weights. No return-alpha result established here.
Independent_verification: Source reviewed; no independent replication or BNY backtest performed
Historical_data_access: FRED NFCI/ANFCI and Chicago Fed downloads public, history back to 1971. ALFRED vintage coverage must be verified.
Point_in_time_requirements: Join by weekly publication date; current entire history may revise. ANFCI additionally conditions on growth/inflation.
Monthly_MVP_fit: Numerically easy; may already be present according to prior project summaries.
Incremental_information: High overlap with possible existing ANFCI and with credit/VIX; establish actual feature list first.
Main_limitations: Revised-history leakage; composite redundancy; crisis dominance; changing weights.
Causal_RAG_role: Explain the underlying component changes; do not claim an index number establishes a unique causal channel.

Decision: Defer; data and specification cost
Authors: Elena Sueppel; Ralph Sueppel
Economic_intuition: Unsterilized interventions can alter reserves and portfolio demand with lags.
Required_inputs: Dated central-bank intervention accounts, monetary base, contemporaneous GDP and multi-horizon changes; comparable country classifications.
Construction: Source core: if changes in intervention accounts I and monetary base B have same sign, L=sign(dI)*min(abs(dI),abs(dB))/GDP, otherwise 0. Source combines annualized multi-horizon values; full horizon/aggregation specification requires notebook.
Definition_status: Core rule verified; full trading construction needs further specification
Assets: Equity; rates; FX; original multi-country scope
Horizon: Medium-term trends; monthly feature conceivable
Reported_evidence: Provider reports combined-strategy benefits and uneven single-signal results; notebook requires JPMaQS access. No independent validation here.
Independent_verification: Source reviewed; no independent replication or BNY backtest performed
Historical_data_access: Central bank statements public but harmonized point-in-time series is JPMaQS. Academic support/trial is a possible route, not confirmed access.
Point_in_time_requirements: Balance-sheet publication dates and GDP denominator vintages essential; total assets alone is not intervention liquidity.
Monthly_MVP_fit: High effort; avoid in first sprint.
Incremental_information: Could add a monetary-quantity channel beyond policy surprises, if not already in liquidity inputs.
Main_limitations: Sterilization and reserve-demand changes; denominator revisions; patchy regimes; proprietary reconstruction; global-to-US transfer.
Causal_RAG_role: Useful for checking operation purpose and whether liquidity is sterilized; do not equate this with an unsupported Fed assets-minus-TGA-minus-RRP chart.

Decision: Required conventional control, not first alpha recommendation
Authors: Tobias J. Moskowitz; Yao Hua Ooi; Lasse Heje Pedersen
Economic_intuition: Gradual information diffusion and investor behavior can sustain trends across markets.
Required_inputs: Existing asset total-return series and risk-free returns, 12 prior months; daily/monthly volatility only if matching source strategy.
Construction: Simple feature x_(a,m)=sum_{k=0..11} log(1+r_excess_(a,m-k)); paper strategy trades sign of prior 12-month excess return with volatility scaling. Our continuous feature is a control, not the original futures strategy.
Definition_status: Original sign strategy known; continuous Ridge control proposed
Assets: Existing equity; duration; USD assets; avoid expanding universe
Horizon: 12-month lookback, 1-month holding
Reported_evidence: Original diversified futures evidence and public 1985–2009 factor data. Kim–Tse–Wald (2016) challenge attribution by highlighting volatility scaling; test matched-risk controls.
Independent_verification: Source reviewed; no independent replication or BNY backtest performed
Historical_data_access: https://www.aqr.com/Insights/Datasets/Time-Series-Momentum-Original-Paper-Data ; reuse team asset returns for BNY feature; original factor is a reference, not underlying instrument history.
Point_in_time_requirements: Use only completed past returns and contemporaneous cash rate. Confirm dividends, futures rolls and FX conventions.
Monthly_MVP_fit: Low if total returns exist; no language model needed.
Incremental_information: Price-based rather than macro-surprise information; useful control for whether new macro signals merely capture trend.
Main_limitations: Whipsaw/reversal; futures-to-ETF transfer; volatility-scaling confound; transaction costs; long/short versus constrained portfolio.
Causal_RAG_role: Low added value for construction; use as a demanding numerical baseline for agent claims.

Decision: Reserve; universe/data dependent
Authors: Ralph S. J. Koijen; Tobias J. Moskowitz; Lasse H. Pedersen; Evert B. Vrugt
Economic_intuition: An asset can offer expected income/roll return even if market conditions do not change.
Required_inputs: Instrument-specific income and financing: bond curve/coupon/duration, FX spot+forward, or commodity futures curve.
Construction: Original definition: expected return under unchanged market conditions. Example FX carry over horizon h: (S_t-F_(t,h))/F_(t,h), with S and F quoted domestic currency per foreign currency. Bond yield-minus-cash alone omits roll, duration and convexity; define instrument carry before testing.
Definition_status: Source definition; exact implementation requires instrument specification
Assets: FX; bonds; commodities, only where universe allows
Horizon: Monthly rebalance; medium term
Reported_evidence: Peer-reviewed multi-asset evidence; not a validation of an ETF dividend-yield proxy.
Independent_verification: Source reviewed; no independent replication or BNY backtest performed
Historical_data_access: Treasury curves public; historical FX forwards/futures chains usually require provider/export. Existing asset price history alone insufficient.
Point_in_time_requirements: Use contemporaneous forward/curve quotes, financing and contract calendars; avoid continuous-futures roll leakage.
Monthly_MVP_fit: Moderate/high depending on actual instruments; defer until universe confirmed.
Incremental_information: Potential income channel beyond release surprises; likely interacts with growth/volatility.
Main_limitations: Crash exposure; funding/transaction costs; quote convention errors; limits to long/short implementation.
Causal_RAG_role: Context on funding and policy regimes may help; RAG should not calculate unobserved forward quotes.

Decision: Reserve; cycle control, likely growth overlap
Authors: Claudia Sahm; Federal Reserve Bank of St. Louis real-time series
Economic_intuition: Broad labor-market deterioration signals weakening demand and recession risk.
Required_inputs: First-release unemployment rate and release dates, or SAHMREALTIME.
Construction: Original rule gap=3-month average U3 minus minimum of 3-month averages over prior 12 months; trigger at 0.50 percentage points. Proposed continuous gap feature avoids fitting a new trading threshold.
Definition_status: Official rule; continuous return-predictor use proposed
Horizon: Recession onset indicator; proposed next-month forecast
Reported_evidence: Designed for recession detection/fiscal response, not established portfolio timing alpha.
Independent_verification: Source reviewed; no independent replication or BNY backtest performed
Historical_data_access: https://fred.stlouisfed.org/series/SAHMREALTIME ; prefer real-time series over SAHMCURRENT. Audit pre-publication reconstruction and vintage coverage.
Point_in_time_requirements: Released unemployment month is lagged; do not label observation month as decision availability. Historical reconstructed rule is not evidence of historical live implementation.
Monthly_MVP_fit: Low; may reuse labor data if first prints preserved.
Incremental_information: High overlap with jobs surprises/growth; level deterioration differs from surprise but may not add value.
Main_limitations: Late equity-market timing; structural labor changes; revisions; few independent recessions.
Causal_RAG_role: Help assess demand slowdown versus labor-supply changes with dated evidence, not retrospective recession labels.

Decision: Reserve; uncertain US-portfolio incremental value
Authors: Boris Hofmann; Ilhyock Shim; Hyun Song Shin
Economic_intuition: Dollar appreciation can tighten dollar-borrower balance sheets and global risk-taking.
Required_inputs: Broad nominal trade-weighted US dollar DTWEXBGS; optional EM sovereign/FX returns only if already in universe.
Construction: Proposed x_m=log(DTWEXBGS_m/DTWEXBGS_(m-3)). This is a market-pressure proxy, not the paper’s empirical identification.
Definition_status: Proposed proxy; mechanism paper is not this trading rule
Assets: Global risk assets; EM rates/FX; USD
Horizon: Monthly/quarterly economic channel; next-month test exploratory
